children.summary: This section is the title slide for Meta's Q1 2026 Earnings Presentation, indicating the start of a financial report for that quarter.

children.title: Advertising Revenue by User Geography
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Earnings Presentation.pdf/Root/Advertising Revenue by User Geography
children.summary: The page displays a stacked bar chart titled 'Advertising Revenue by User Geography' from Meta, showing revenue in millions across nine quarters from Q1'24 to Q1'26. The data is segmented into four geographic regions: US & Canada, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Rest of World. Key standout values include the highest total revenue of $58,137 million in Q4'25 and the lowest of $35,635 million in Q1'24.

children.title: Revenue by User Geography
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Earnings Presentation.pdf/Root/Revenue by User Geography
children.summary: The page displays a stacked bar chart titled 'Revenue by User Geography' from Meta, showing financial data in millions. The chart covers nine quarters from Q1'24 to Q1'26 and breaks down total revenue into four geographic segments: US & Canada, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Rest of World. Key standout values include the highest total revenue of $59,893 million in Q4'25 and the lowest of $36,455 million in Q1'24.

children.title: Segment Results
children.summary: This page displays Meta's financial Segment Results in a table format, covering quarterly data from Q1'24 through Q1'26. The top section details revenue breakdowns for Advertising, Other, Family of Apps Revenue, and Reality Labs Revenue, culminating in Total Revenue. The bottom section outlines operating income metrics, including Family of Apps Operating Income, Reality Labs Operating Loss, Total Income from Operations, and Operating Margin percentages.

children.title: Expenses as a Percentage of Revenue
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Earnings Presentation.pdf/Root/Expenses as a Percentage of Revenue
children.summary: The page displays a stacked bar chart titled 'Expenses as a Percentage of Revenue' for Meta, covering the period from Q1 2024 to Q1 2026. The chart breaks down expenses into four categories: Cost of Revenue, Research & Development, Marketing & Sales, and General & Administrative. Key standout values include R&D expenses peaking at 31% in Q1 2026 and G&A expenses dropping significantly to 2% in Q4 2024.

children.title: Effective Tax Rate
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Earnings Presentation.pdf/Root/Effective Tax Rate
children.summary: This page displays a financial table titled 'Effective Tax Rate' for Meta, covering quarterly data from Q1 2024 through Q1 2026. The table presents three key metrics: 'Income before income taxes', 'Provision (benefit) for income taxes', and the resulting 'Effective Tax Rate'. Notable figures include an effective tax rate of 87% in Q3 2025 and a negative rate of (23)% in Q1 2026. Footnotes explain that these anomalies are due to one-time charges related to the 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act' and benefits from U.S. Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax transitional relief.

children.title: Net Income
children.summary: The page displays a bar chart titled 'Net Income' for Meta, showing financial data in millions of dollars across nine quarters from Q1 2024 to Q1 2026. The chart highlights significant fluctuations, including a sharp dip in Q3 2025 and a peak in Q1 2026. Footnotes explain that the Q3 2025 low was due to a one-time tax charge related to the 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act', while the Q1 2026 high included a tax benefit under Treasury Notice 2026-7.

children.title: Diluted Earnings Per Share
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Earnings Presentation.pdf/Root/Diluted Earnings Per Share
children.summary: The page displays a bar chart titled 'Diluted Earnings Per Share' for Meta, covering the period from Q1 2024 to Q1 2026. The chart illustrates quarterly earnings per share (EPS), showing values ranging from $1.05 in Q3 2025 to a high of $10.44 in Q1 2026. Footnotes explain that the Q3 2025 figure includes a one-time tax charge related to the 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act', while the Q1 2026 figure includes a tax benefit under Treasury Notice 2026-7.

children.title: Capital Expenditures
children.summary: The page displays a bar chart titled 'Capital Expenditures' for the company Meta, with values presented in millions. The chart compares quarterly expenditures for Q1'25 ($13,692) and Q1'26 ($19,840) against annual projections for 2024 ($39,225) and 2025 ($72,215). A footnote clarifies that these figures relate to purchases of property, equipment, and principal payments on finance leases.

children.title: Family Daily Active People (DAP)
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Earnings Presentation.pdf/Root/Family Daily Active People (DAP)
children.summary: The page displays a bar chart titled 'Family Daily Active People (DAP)' showing data in billions from Q1'24 to Q1'26. The chart illustrates a steady growth trend, peaking at 3.58 billion in Q4'25 before a slight decline to 3.56 billion in Q1'26. Footnotes explain that the Q1'26 decline was due to internet disruptions in Iran and restrictions on WhatsApp in Russia. Additional text defines DAP as users of Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, or WhatsApp and details the methodology for counting unique individuals across these platforms.

children.title: Family Average Revenue per Person (ARPP)
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Earnings Presentation.pdf/Root/Family Average Revenue per Person (ARPP)
children.summary: The page displays a bar chart titled 'Family Average Revenue per Person (ARPP)' from Meta, illustrating revenue trends across nine quarters from Q1'24 to Q1'26. The chart shows fluctuating values, with the highest point at $16.56 in Q4'25 and the lowest at $11.20 in Q1'24. A footnote defines ARPP as FoA revenue divided by the average number of DAP during a quarter.

children.title: Ad Impressions Delivered YoY Percentage Change
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Earnings Presentation.pdf/Root/Ad Impressions Delivered YoY Percentage Change
children.summary: This page displays a series of bar charts titled 'Ad Impressions Delivered YoY Percentage Change' from Meta. The data is segmented by five geographic regions: Worldwide, US & Canada, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Rest of World. Each chart illustrates the year-over-year percentage growth in ad impressions across five quarters, ranging from Q1'25 to Q1'26.

children.title: Average Price Per Ad YoY Percentage Change
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Earnings Presentation.pdf/Root/Average Price Per Ad YoY Percentage Change
children.summary: The page displays five bar charts illustrating the Year-over-Year (YoY) Percentage Change in Average Price Per Ad for Meta across different geographic regions: Worldwide, US & Canada, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Rest of World. The data covers quarterly periods from Q1'25 through Q1'26. Standout values include a 20% increase in the Rest of World region during Q3'25 and a negative growth of (2)% in the Asia-Pacific region during Q4'25.

children.title: Appendix
children.summary: This page serves as a section header for an appendix, indicated by the large text 'Appendix' on the left side. The bottom right corner features the logo of the organization Meta.

children.title: Free Cash Flow Reconciliation
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Earnings Presentation.pdf/Root/Appendix/Free Cash Flow Reconciliation
children.summary: The page displays a financial table titled 'Free Cash Flow Reconciliation' for Meta, with values presented in millions. The table details the calculation of Free Cash Flow (FCF) by starting with net cash provided by operating activities and subtracting purchases of property and equipment as well as principal payments on finance leases. It covers quarterly data from Q1'24 through Q1'26, showing a trend where FCF fluctuates between approximately $8.5 billion and $15.5 billion over the period.

children.title: Limitations of Key Metrics and Other Data
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Earnings Presentation.pdf/Root/Appendix/Limitations of Key Metrics and Other Data

children.title: Family Metrics
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Earnings Presentation.pdf/Root/Appendix/Limitations of Key Metrics and Other Data/Family Metrics
children.summary: This page, titled 'Limitations of Key Metrics and Other Data' from Meta, details the methodology and inherent challenges in calculating 'Family metrics,' which include Daily Active People (DAP) and Average Revenue Per Person (ARPP). It explains that these figures are estimates based on internal data for users across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, and WhatsApp. The text highlights that due to complex attribution techniques and statistical variances, there is an estimated error margin of approximately 3% for worldwide DAP.

children.title: User Geography
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Earnings Presentation.pdf/Root/Appendix/Limitations of Key Metrics and Other Data/User Geography
children.summary: This section explains that estimates for revenue by user location and ad impressions are affected by data limitations in measuring user geography. It states that user location is estimated based on factors like IP address and self-disclosed location, which may not always reflect the actual location (e.g., due to proxy servers).
